title: Rotate String
statement:
Given two strings `s` and `goal`, return `true` if and only if `s` can become `goal` after some number of shifts on `s`.

A shift on `s` consists of moving the leftmost character of `s` to the rightmost position. For example, if `s = "abcde"`, then it will be "bcdea" after one shift.
constraints: s and goal consist of lowercase English letters.

editorial.approach: Verify that s and goal have identical lengths first. If so, check if goal is a substring of s + s. If it is, return true, otherwise false.

hints: If the lengths of `s` and `goal` are different, they cannot be equal after any shifts.
If you concatenate `s` with itself (`s + s`), what substrings can you find in it?
Every possible shift of `s` is a substring of `s + s`. Check if `goal` is a substring of `s + s`.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Simulate each of the `n` possible shifts of `s` and compare the shifted string to `goal`.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Concatenate `s` with itself (`s + s`). All possible rotations of `s` are substrings of `s + s`. If `goal` matches in length and is a substring of `s + s`, return true.

interviewExplanation: Simulating all shifts takes quadratic time. We optimize it to linear O(n) time by concatenating `s` with `s`. The string `s + s` contains all circular shift variants of `s` as contiguous substrings of length `n`.
